market_holds: Sealed baseline (18:10 UTC): spot $15.155, event-implied move 14.8% (front straddle 16.2%), skew balanced (+0.3 vol pts), put/call OI 0.41 (call-heavy). Run-up +20.8% over 5 sessions and +26.9% over 20, almost all of it today: the stock was +16.7% at $15.10 by 13:55 ET (Motley Fool, 2026-11-09) against S&P +2.4% and Nasdaq +2.6% on the same day. Stated reasons are the co-founder Dave Pickles CTO-council announcement (company release 2026-11-03), a sector-wide ad-tech rally and pre-print positioning. The shares were at about $12.29, near the 52-week low of $11.62, a week earlier (MarketBeat, 2026-11-02). Q3 consensus is $651.4m revenue and $0.25 EPS (Yahoo, 32 revenue analysts; 17 EPS cuts in 90 days, flat over the last 60). That sits on the company's floor of at least $650m (-12% y/y) and adjusted EBITDA of about $160m. Q4 consensus is $691.6m (-18% y/y; range $660m-$819m) and $0.29 EPS (Yahoo). BusinessQuant has $704.6m, undated. Press framing (Motley Fool, 2026-11-08) puts the bar higher: a Q4 floor of about $745m, i.e. no worse than Q3's -12%, would signal that the declines are easing, so the buy-side bar sits between about $692m and $745m. Last eight reactions: 7 down and 1 up, median absolute move 13%, including -21.9% on the Q3 guide in August 2026 and -38.6% in August 2025. The stock trades on the guide, not the quarter. Short interest was about 16% of float on 2026-08-20 (Equibles aggregator, rising). No newer figure was found.
view: TTD's problem is company-specific share and take-rate loss in a healthy ad market. Magnite's CTV grew 39% in Q3 and it raised guidance. Viant grew 34% in Q2. Amazon guides its ad revenue to high-teens growth in Q4. TTD meanwhile guided Q3 to -12% y/y after +3% in Q2. The release will be judged on the Q4 guide. Two forces pull against each other. For an upside surprise: the sell-side Q4 number of $692m implies only +6% from Q3 to Q4 against +15% to +23% in each of the last three years. On a two-year stack it implies a 10-point deterioration from Q3's +4% to about -7%. October's midterm political spend, which Magnite says came in near 3x its forecast, falls in TTD's Q4 against an off-year Q4 2025. So a floor in the $700-720m range is plausible and would beat the sell-side mean. Against: the buy side already wanted more, about $745m on the Fool's -12% framing, and the stock gained about 14 points relative to the market today, roughly one implied move. Much of a relief outcome is therefore already in the price at entry. The new CFO told the August call that the Q3 weakness 'probably' continues into Q4 and that guidance would be 'credible' and 'grounded in the data'. Trade press reports fee concessions and post-auction discounts tied to quarterly spend thresholds, which hit net revenue hardest in Q4, the biggest spend quarter. TTD's floors have lately landed at or below the actual (Q2 missed its own floor by $35m), and seven of the last eight prints fell. On balance I lean slightly down: a floor that beats $692m but falls short of about $745m is the modal outcome, and after a 17% pre-print ramp it reads as a disappointment. A crowded short near record-low multiples, plus possible buyback or OpenAI/agentic headlines, could still produce a squeeze. The lean is too weak to act on.

recommendation.reason: The mechanisms I can find cancel each other. A sell-side Q4 bar ($692m, -18% y/y) that looks too low on seasonality and the midterm political spend sits against a same-day run of about 14 points relative to the market, which already holds a relief outcome. Reported fee concessions should weigh hardest on net revenue in Q4. I found no dated, independent datapoint since the August call that tells me where the Q4 floor lands relative to the roughly $745m buy-side bar. Without one, probability does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 revenue floor at or above about $745m (y/y decline no worse than Q3's -12%), especially with a larger buyback, would make the gap up likely despite today's run. A floor below about $700m would make a large gap down likely.

self_critique: The strongest case for up: the sell-side Q4 mean of -18% may be a bar the company clears with room once October's midterm political spend and the cost cuts land. The stock is at a record-low multiple with about 16% of float short. A 'better than feared' floor plus a buyback could squeeze it well beyond today's gain. The strongest case for a bigger down call: the run-up is about one implied move, and a seven-in-eight record of guide disappointment would argue for more than 58% down. I did not push further either way because I found no dated data on TTD's own Q4 trajectory.
approach_notes: P4 (prove 'priced in') helped most: it pushed me to quantify the Q4 bar and compare it with seasonality, which showed a sell-side vs buy-side gap rather than a plain stale estimate. P3's worker and physical sources had little traction for a DSP with no public spend series since the August call.
